summary: Preserve SFTP write failures instead of reporting false retained-work conflicts. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: SFTP is an advertised destination. The fix only makes a denied write report its real permission error instead of a false conflict; the existing SFTP troubleshooting already tells operators to check the account's rights, so no step changes.

api.reason: A failed SFTP owner or publication write now reports the underlying destination error when no conflicting file exists. No route or schema changes; the existing terminal operation result carries the corrected error. Machine-readable response shapes are unchanged.

roadmap.reason: Corrects error reporting within the existing destination fault gate.

state.reason: No new durable record; Core already owns the operation, run, point and SFTP publication intent.

verification.method: A matched disposable OpenSSH target denied writes while allowing reads; the pre-fix backup produced one failed run and no point or staging, but its terminal error falsely said retained-work conflict. The focused in-process SFTP regression failed before the fix and passed afterward for owner claim, first intent write and exact intent retry. Focused race and the full agent package passed; independent read-only source review found no remaining concrete issue after the resumed-publication correction. A matched fixed-build OpenSSH retest then returned one failed run with permission denied, no point or staging, and the same result on exact replay. Its protected two-disk control restored and verified under denial; typed cleanup removed the VM/pin, health recovered, and original point/source hashes matched. Forge CI remains open.
verification.limits: The native write denial used a controlled OpenSSH directory mode. Abrupt server loss, full-target exhaustion and final-publication faults remain open.
